page: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512g-3840s is a memory-optimized server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 3840 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top tier for single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and overall PassMark CPU score, which includes extended instructions and physics tests. Multi-core CPU performance and CPU encryption tests rank in the strong category. Memory performance is highly competitive, with large-block read and write bandwidths scoring in the top tier, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. The system also demonstrates top-tier efficiency in single-threaded gzip compression and both single- and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the vx1-m-64c-512g-3840s is its shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated-core instances. However, this shared model offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring massive memory density and substantial NVMe storage without requiring continuous, dedicated 100% CPU utilization. The instance excels in database operations, scoring in the top tier for PassMark database benchmarks, and shows strong performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving. It is also highly capable for medium-scale LLM inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds with 7B parameter models.
description: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512g-3840s is a memory-optimized server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring 64 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM on an AMD EPYC x86_64 platform. The instance includes 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates on a shared CPU allocation model. In benchmark testing, it delivers top-tier performance in single-core processing, large-block memory bandwidth, and database operations, alongside strong multi-core and static web serving capabilities. While the shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for sustained compute-intensive tasks, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial NVMe storage make it a highly cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads. It is well-suited for database hosting, Redis deployments, large-scale data processing, and medium-scale LLM inference.
